blocks.body: # 100 Workbenches for a Reproducible Human–AI Research Factory

## The portfolio is practical enough to launch

**The result is 100 workbench contracts, not 100 vague topics:** 94 are practical improvement frontiers with machine-checkable or physically measurable gates, and six are the still-open Clay problems in a separate exact-proof lane. Every practical row asks two questions in order: *is it correct and safe?* and only then *is it a useful Pareto improvement after time, memory, energy and money are counted?*

Two unrelated people must each own a blind reproduction before promotion. A failed attempt is still admitted to the searchable attempt graph when its scope, artifacts and failure are reproducible; it simply does not enter the verified-solution repository.

## Most of the factory can produce useful evidence immediately

The portfolio deliberately weights digital optimisation and standardized engineering tests, where a worker can compare a candidate with a pinned baseline without anyone voting on whether the output *looks clever*. The six proof problems are visible but isolated so their prestige cannot weaken the ordinary admission standard.

## A workbench is a versioned measurement contract

Each workbench freezes: the question and scope; public development inputs; sealed holdouts; dataset and environment hashes; a correctness/safety verifier; baseline artifacts; primary and secondary metrics; tolerances or statistical tests; resource ceilings; an economic or physical guardrail; and the evidence bundle required for reproduction.

**Better** means a new non-dominated point after every hard gate passes. It does not mean winning one metric by spending absurd compute or shifting cost elsewhere. Exact outputs use zero tolerance; runtimes use controlled repeated measurements; stochastic results use predeclared seeds and uncertainty; physical results use calibrated uncertainty and replicate specimens.

## Promotion is blind, two-person and failure-aware

1. The author freezes code, method, environment, data hashes, claimed result and cost vector.
2. The evaluator hides both the claim and holdout answers.
3. Two unrelated human owners independently rerun the locked artifact without seeing one another's result.
4. The evaluator checks hard gates, then compares results under the workbench's predeclared rule.
5. Two passes make the candidate eligible for the verified repository; disagreement goes to a blind tie-break and divergence review.
6. Reproducible dead ends enter the attempt graph as `RERUN_CONFIRMED_NO_GAIN`, `BOUNDARY_FOUND` or another typed negative result. `UNRUNNABLE`, `INVALID` and `DISPUTED` remain distinct states.

## Compression & storage

These are ideal first-floor workbenches: correctness can be exact, benchmark files can be hashed, and the commercial question can be expressed as storage plus compute cost per retained or delivered unit.

## Routing & logistics

Feasibility is checked before distance or makespan. A shorter route, denser pack or faster schedule is invalid if it breaks capacity, time, safety or staffing constraints.

## Communications & sensing

Accuracy is only one axis. Every candidate also carries latency, memory, power, hardware and subgroup or operating-condition gates.

## Software & compute

These workbenches pair exact outputs or official validators with performance, tail latency, memory, energy and price/performance measurements.

## Energy, power & thermal

Simulation is the first gate, not the last. Promotion to deployment requires hardware or laboratory evidence plus reliability, degradation and lifecycle-cost checks.

## Manufacturing & materials

The unit of value is a conforming, durable part or recovered material—not a single flattering coupon, image or classifier score.

## Water, environment & civil

These require mass balance, uncertainty and failure-mode accounting. Field claims remain in a separate lane until replicated outside the development site or season.

## Robotics & transport

Safety constraints are non-tradeable. Simulation can rank candidates, but physical promotion needs controlled trials before any operational use.

## Clay exact proofs

These six use exact logical gates. The four-hour pack tests discipline and vocabulary, not credentials; passing it grants permission to submit work, not scientific credibility or a prize claim.

## The Clay lane must never imply that the platform awards a proof

The starter pack is a seriousness and scientific-hygiene gate, not an intelligence test and not a credential test. Target about four hours on free Colab-class compute, provide an accessibility/time alternative, and ask the entrant to reproduce a known result, catch a planted invalid inference, preserve a signed log, and distinguish finite evidence from a universal theorem.

After that, a proposed solution still needs an exact theorem statement, definitions, lemma dependency graph, citation and assumption audit, adversarial counterexample search, formalization where feasible, two independent human-owned reproductions and specialist review. Clay's own process remains authoritative: CMI does not accept direct submissions and requires qualifying publication, at least two years, and general acceptance before it will consider a solution.

## The gates remove nonsense; they do not remove experimental reality

A frozen benchmark can be overfit, so each practical lane needs rotating sealed holdouts and later out-of-distribution or field confirmation. Physical work also needs laboratories, calibrated instruments and enough replicate units to estimate variance. A candidate that wins in simulation is labelled *simulation-verified*, not *field-verified*. Medical, infrastructure and safety-critical outputs remain non-deployable until their separate regulatory and safety processes are satisfied.

The list is a launch portfolio, not a claim that these are the only worthwhile questions or that every benchmark is permanent. Workbench versions should be retired when saturated, leaked or no longer economically representative.

## Start with three workbenches that exercise different evidence types

1. **General-purpose lossless compression:** exact round trip, cheap runners and an immediately understandable cost model.
2. **Capacitated vehicle routing:** exact feasibility plus a multi-objective distance/time/compute frontier.
3. **NIST additive-manufacturing prediction:** a genuinely physical blind benchmark that tests the hand-off from computation to laboratory truth.

Build one shared `workbench.yaml` schema and evaluator, then instantiate those three. Do not build 100 bespoke platforms first; prove that one admission protocol can carry three very different truth conditions.

## Decisions for the first repository version

- Which three workbenches receive launch maintainers and compute budget?
- What minimum economic improvement is meaningful in each lane: a fixed percentage, a confidence-bound gain, or any strict Pareto improvement?
- How often are hidden holdouts rotated, and who is allowed to construct them?
- Which negative-result types are strong enough to prevent agents repeating the same search region?
- Which identity check is proportionate for ordinary work, and when should organizational separation be required?

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: SHA-256-identical reconstruction on every public and hidden file; measure compressed bytes, encode/decode throughput, peak RAM and joules. Promote only a smaller/faster Pareto point against pinned zstd, xz and other verified anchors.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: total CPU, energy and storage cost per retained TB must fall, with a deployable decoder.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: exact enwik9 restoration, with compressor/decompressor size, runtime and memory accounted exactly under the challenge rules.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: compute cost must be justified by archive lifetime and retrieval frequency; prohibit “tiny archive, week-long decoder” claims from being presented as general deployment wins.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: CRAM-conformant files whose decoded records, tags, qualities and reference identifiers match the canonical input; verify indexed random access as well as full decoding. Measure bytes/read, encoding, decoding, memory and range-read latency against CRAM 3.1 profiles.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: storage and egress savings must exceed added CPU and reference-management cost.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: every value respects the declared absolute/relative error bound; additionally freeze domain-specific quantities of interest so a compressor cannot preserve PSNR while corrupting the scientific result. Measure ratio, throughput, RAM, PSNR/NRMSE and downstream-error deltas.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: saved storage/I/O time must exceed compression compute and any scientifically acceptable loss.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: conformance to lossless or declared near-lossless bounds, bit-accurate decoding, worst-case memory and deterministic operation; measure bits/pixel, samples/s, latency and energy.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: downlink savings must exceed onboard power, FPGA area and qualification cost; no unbounded memory or unpredictable worst case.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: fixed bitrates on public and hidden CLIC images, valid decoding, objective scores plus the benchmark’s blinded preference procedure, decoder-size cap, latency, RAM and energy.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: report CDN/storage savings per million images net of encode/decode cost; prohibit server-only decoders masquerading as mobile-ready improvements.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: follow the current AOM common test conditions exactly; report BD-rate across required quality metrics, bitstream validity, encode/decode time, peak RAM and energy on every sequence.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: calculate total encode, delivery and playback cost per viewing hour; a gain fails if target devices cannot decode within their power/latency envelope.
category_1.benchmark: AOM AV2 Common Test Conditions v9
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: use MPEG G-PCC common test conditions for lossless and lossy geometry/attribute tracks; verify geometry validity and report bitrate, geometry/color distortion, runtime and memory.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: network/storage savings must exceed edge decode energy and latency, with separate profiles for maps, LiDAR and immersive media.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: sample-for-sample, channel-for-channel PCM recovery across the EBU SQAM material; measure total bytes, streaming startup, seek correctness, encode/decode throughput, RAM and energy against FLAC anchors.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: storage/bandwidth savings must exceed compute cost and retain real-time decoding on inexpensive devices.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: CCSDS-conformant, bit-identical round trip across frozen integer telemetry distributions; include packet-boundary recovery, worst-case expansion, corruption containment, cycles/sample, RAM and latency.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: radio time saved must exceed onboard power and implementation risk; worst-case expansion must fit the link budget.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: retain every MLPerf Tiny task’s prescribed accuracy while measuring executable/model bytes, latency, peak RAM and optional energy on declared hardware; hidden inputs test generalization.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: reduce flash/RAM BOM or energy per inference without shifting an uneconomic retraining or cloud cost elsewhere.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_1.hard_gate_and_score: replay frozen SNIA traces, reconstruct every byte exactly, and test crash recovery; measure physical bytes, read/write latency, CPU, RAM, metadata overhead and write amplification.
category_1.economic_or_physical_guardrail: report cost per usable protected TB and restore SLA; capacity savings do not count if recovery or sustained writes become commercially unacceptable.
category_1.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: verifier confirms one valid tour and exact TSPLIB distance; compare tour length, optimality gap, time, RAM and energy under fixed budgets. Any claimed optimum requires a certificate, not merely the best observed tour.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: compute cost per route must be smaller than the saved travel value.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: all customers served once, depot and vehicle-capacity constraints satisfied, and cost recalculated by the canonical CVRPLIB convention; report fleet size, distance, gap and compute.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: fuel/labour savings must exceed planning cost, and an algorithm must finish inside the real dispatch window.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: independently verify capacity, service times, arrival windows and SINTEF’s hierarchical vehicle-count/distance objective; report feasibility rate, fleet, distance and compute across Solomon and Homberger instances.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: value lateness and vehicles explicitly, and reject solutions too slow for daily replanning.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: every request’s pickup precedes its matched delivery, vehicle loads remain legal and all time windows hold; use SINTEF’s checker and report vehicles, distance, gap and runtime.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: planning compute plus deadheading must be less than saved fleet/labour cost.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: train only on the published split and evaluate blindly on held-out Amazon routes; measure official sequence score, route time and compute, with package and time-window feasibility checked separately.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: estimate minutes, miles and cloud cost per route; improvements must survive multiple cities rather than one depot.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: replay frozen NYC TLC days chronologically so future requests cannot leak backward; verify capacity and pickup/drop-off order, then measure wait time, detour, rejected trips, empty kilometres, p95 service and compute.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: net revenue, driver utilization and passenger cost must improve after dispatch compute and repositioning.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.workbench: One-dimensional bin packing and cutting stock
category_2.hard_gate_and_score: every item appears exactly once, no bin exceeds capacity, and bin count/waste is recalculated by an independent verifier; report gap and solve time across BPPLIB.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: material/container savings must exceed solver time and operational complexity.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: validate dimensions, rotations, non-overlap, stock boundaries, kerf and any guillotine restrictions; measure sheets used, waste area, cut length and compute on standardized instances.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: material and machine-time savings must exceed planning and additional toolpath/setup cost.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: independently verify orientation rules, containment, non-overlap, weight, support, stacking and centre-of-mass constraints; measure containers, volume utilization, damage-risk proxies and runtime.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: freight savings must exceed planning and handling complexity; physically unstable arrangements are invalid regardless of volume.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: each operation uses its required machine once, precedence holds and machine intervals never overlap; independently recalculate makespan and gap across JSPLib.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: saved machine/labour time must exceed scheduling compute and rescheduling disruption; include a fixed short-response track.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: preserve each job’s machine order and non-overlap, then verify makespan on the full Taillard sets; report gap, runtime, RAM and schedule stability.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: increased throughput must exceed planning and changeover cost; publish the value of a one-percent makespan reduction for the declared line.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: all precedences and renewable/non-renewable resource limits hold at every time; recalculate makespan and gap on PSPLIB, including multi-mode variants only in their declared lane.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: value earlier completion against compute and schedule churn; prohibit gains obtained through undeclared extra resources.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: zero hard-constraint violations for coverage, qualifications, contracts and rest; recalculate weighted soft penalties, runtime and stability on held-out instances.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: report overtime/agency cost and changed assignments, while imposing non-tradeable safe coverage and fatigue limits.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_2.hard_gate_and_score: zero room, student, lecturer or curriculum conflicts; independently score capacity, spacing, compactness and stability penalties under the frozen ITC definition.
category_2.economic_or_physical_guardrail: reduce rooms, disruption and administrative time without degrading accessibility or creating impractical late schedules.
category_2.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: reproduce BER/FER curves at frozen code/rate/channel/SNR points and known vectors; report throughput, latency, RAM and joules/decoded bit against AFF3CT anchors.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: improved reliability or throughput must justify silicon area, power and implementation complexity.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: use frozen 5G NR PUSCH and ray-traced/stochastic channel configurations; report BLER/BER, spectral efficiency, throughput, latency, compute and power, with standards-conformant transmitted data.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: gains must fit UE/base-station real-time and power budgets without excessive pilot overhead or specialist hardware.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: chronological replay and then randomized live trials where possible; measure delivered quality, rebuffer time, startup delay, quality switches, latency and bytes, with confidence intervals because network outcomes are heavy-tailed.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: CDN/compute cost per viewing hour and abandonment must both improve.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: frozen DNS development plus hidden clips; measure standardized SIG, BAK and overall quality, word accuracy, causal latency and real-time factor.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: report cloud/device cost, bandwidth and battery per audio hour; non-causal or oversized models cannot enter the real-time lane.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: evaluate blind machine types and domains using AUC, pAUC, precision, recall and F1; measure false alarms, inference latency, model size and energy.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: combine missed-failure and false-maintenance costs, and require deployment cost below the expected avoided downtime.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: use untouched SIDD benchmark pairs; report raw and sRGB PSNR/SSIM, colour error, latency, RAM, model size and energy, with no test-image adaptation.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: meet camera-pipeline frame deadlines and mobile power/memory limits; server-sized improvements remain in an exploratory lane.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: first meet the frozen DIV2K/LSDIR PSNR threshold, then minimize runtime, parameters, FLOPs, RAM and energy on fixed hardware; verify output dimensions and prohibit hidden-test training.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: must meet a declared phone, TV or edge latency/power profile rather than win through model size.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: KITTI’s hidden evaluator recomputes endpoint error and outlier rates; also report runtime, failure rate, RAM and energy across the complete set.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: meet the sensor frame deadline on priced hardware; accuracy gains that require an uneconomic GPU or miss real-time operation are separate Pareto points.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: run EuRoC sequences from raw camera/IMU inputs without future leakage; align trajectories by the declared convention and report translation/rotation error, drift, tracking failures, latency and power.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: improve positioning per watt and hardware pound/dollar while sustaining real-time operation; external map/services must be costed.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_3.hard_gate_and_score: use the official nuScenes split and evaluator; report NDS/mAP plus per-class, distance, weather and lighting results, latency, RAM and energy.
category_3.economic_or_physical_guardrail: state sensor and compute BOM, watts and frame deadline; promotion requires minimum safety-critical subgroup performance, not only a higher average.
category_3.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_4.economic_or_physical_guardrail: compute-hour/energy savings must exceed added compilation time and binary footprint.
category_4.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

category_4.economic_or_physical_guardrail: translate improvements into flash/RAM BOM, battery life and build-time cost.
category_4.starter_pack: Reproduce the pinned baseline, pass the public verifier, then submit one sealed candidate against hidden holdouts.

query.sql: SELECT w.* FROM (SELECT UNNEST(workbenches) AS w FROM read_json_auto('research_factory_100_workbenches.json'))
query.description: A curated synthesis of 94 benchmarkable practical improvement workbenches and the six unresolved Clay Millennium Prize Problems, frozen on 1 August 2026.
filters: Practical problems require an external verifier and economic or physical guardrail
Clay lane contains only the six problems listed as unsolved by CMI
metric_definitions: Total workbenches = count of distinct sequential workbench IDs.
Practical workbenches = entries 1–94 with measurable performance and cost or physical constraints.
Exact-proof workbenches = the six Clay problems officially listed as unsolved on 1 August 2026.

query.description: Official current list of the six unresolved Millennium Prize Problems.
Official rules for external publication, waiting period and general acceptance.
